items.statement: A filtered (ϕ,N,G_K)-module over K is weakly admissible if it is semistable of slope 0, a reformulation due to Faltings of Fontaine's original notion, and acyclic if its Harder–Narasimhan slopes are ≥ 0. A weakly admissible module is acyclic, and conversely an acyclic module is weakly admissible if and only if it is of degree 0.
items.note: "Acyclic" is introduced here; §3 announces it as a notion that will play an important role later in the paper.

items.name: Lemma 5.3: acyclic ⟺ admits a smaller weakly admissible filtration
items.statement: For a filtered (ϕ,N,G_K)-module (M,Fil^•) over K the following are equivalent: (a) it is acyclic; (b) there is a filtration Fil^•_1 on M_K with Fil^i_1M_K ⊂ Fil^iM_K for all i and (M,Fil^•_1) weakly admissible. For (a)⇒(b) it suffices to shrink the filtration at one step while keeping acyclicity, since the degree then drops strictly and the process terminates at degree 0, i.e. at slope 0. To do so, let M_1 be the largest subobject of slope 0 and M_2 = M/M_1, which has slope > 0; shrinking any one graded piece of the filtration on M_2 by one dimension decreases the degree of every subobject by at most 1, so keeps all slopes ≥ 0, and pulling back gives the required Fil^•_1. The converse is immediate, the slope of (M,Fil^•) being at least that of (M,Fil^•_1).
items.note: The argument requires that shrinking the filtration decrease the degree, i.e. deg = t_H − t_N. The same argument is reused in Remark 5.14(iii) and, adapted to C, in Proposition 5.23.

items.name: Lemma 5.4: a weakly admissible subfiltration with the same bounds
items.statement: For (M,Fil^•) acyclic over K with ϕ-slopes in [0,r], Fil^0M_K = M_K and Fil^{r+1}M_K = 0, there is Fil^•_1 with (M,Fil^•_1) weakly admissible, Fil^i_1M_K ⊂ Fil^iM_K for all i, Fil^0_1M_K = M_K and Fil^{r+1}_1M_K = 0. In the proof of Lemma 5.3 the ϕ-slopes of M_2 lie in [0,r], and deg(M_2) > 0 forces Fil^1M_K ≠ 0; taking i_0 largest with Fil^{i_0}M_K ≠ 0 and shrinking Fil^{i_0} by codimension 1 keeps acyclicity and the two boundary conditions while dropping the degree, so iterating gives the filtration.
items.note: The printed definition of the modified filtration reads "Fil^i_1M_K = Fil^iM_K is i ≠ 0", where the index must be i ≠ i_0 — with i ≠ 0 the definition would contradict the preceding clause and destroy Fil^0_1M_K = M_K.

items.name: The fundamental complex and V_st(M,Fil^•)
items.statement: For (M,Fil^•) a filtered (ϕ,N,G_K)-module over K set X_st(M,Fil^•) := (M ⊗_{F^nr} B_st)^{N=0,ϕ=1} and X_dR(M,Fil^•) := (M_K ⊗_K B_dR)/Fil^0(M_K ⊗_K B_dR); these are inductive limits of the X^{(r)} obtained by replacing B_st, B_dR by t^{−r}B^+_st, t^{−r}B^+_dR, which are objects of C(G_K). The complex X_st(M,Fil^•) → X_dR(M,Fil^•) is, following Colmez–Fontaine, the fundamental complex associated to M; its H^0 is written V_st(M,Fil^•), so that 0 → V_st(M,Fil^•) → X_st(M,Fil^•) → X_dR(M,Fil^•) is exact. The filtration on M_K ⊗_K B_dR is the convolution filtration, Fil^0(M_K ⊗_K B_dR) = Σ_n Fil^nM_K ⊗_K t^{−n}B^+_dR.

items.name: Remark 5.5: the fundamental complex, its bundle, and the surjectivity
items.statement: (i) The cohomology of the fundamental complex agrees with that of the truncated complex for r large, so its cohomology groups lie in C(G_K). (ii) The pair (X_st,X_dR) is a B-pair in Berger's sense, with an associated G_K-equivariant vector bundle E(M,Fil^•) on the Fargues–Fontaine curve whose cohomology the fundamental complex computes; since the Harder–Narasimhan slope of E(M,Fil^•) is that of (M,Fil^•), the bundle has vanishing H^1 exactly when (M,Fil^•) is acyclic, in which case 0 → V_st → X_st → X_dR → 0 is exact. (iii) If (M,Fil^•) is acyclic then V_st is a finite dimensional Q_p-vector space precisely when the module is of slope 0, i.e. weakly admissible; this implies admissibility, the natural maps giving V_st ⊗ B_st ≅ M ⊗_F B_st as (ϕ,N)-modules and V_st ⊗ B_dR ≅ M_K ⊗_K B_dR as filtered modules, and V := V_st is then potentially semistable with D_dR(V) = M_K, D_pst(V) = M. (iv) If (M,Fil^•) is acyclic but not admissible, the map V_st ⊗ B^+_dR → Fil^0(M_K ⊗_K B_dR) is not an isomorphism — the kernel is huge — but it is surjective: choosing Fil^•_1 ⊂ Fil^• admissible gives the exact sequence (5.6) 0 → V_st(M,Fil^•_1) → V_st(M,Fil^•) → Fil^0(M_K ⊗ B_dR)/Fil^0_1(M_K ⊗ B_dR) → 0, and B^+_dR·V_st(M,Fil^•) contains B^+_dR·V_st(M,Fil^•_1) = Fil^0_1(M_K ⊗ B_dR).
items.note: (5.6) is the only numbered display of §5 and is used verbatim in the proof of Theorem 5.8. The identification of slopes in (ii) is what pins down the intended sign of the degree in §5.1.2.

items.name: The contravariant functors D^*_st, D^*_dR and D^*_pst on C(G_K)
items.statement: The classical contravariant functors extend to objects of C(G_K), unlike the more commonly used covariant ones. For W ∈ C(G_K) set D^*_st(W) := Hom_{G_K}(W,B_st), a (ϕ,N)-module with ⟨ϕ(µ),v⟩ = ϕ(⟨µ,v⟩) and ⟨N(µ),v⟩ = N(⟨µ,v⟩), and D^*_dR(W) := Hom_{G_K}(W,B_dR), a filtered module with Fil^iD^*_dR(W) = {µ : µ(W) ⊂ t^iB^+_dR}; and D^*_pst(W) := Hom^{sm}_{G_K}(W,B_st) := colim_{[L:K]<∞}Hom_{G_L}(W,B_st), a (ϕ,N,G_K)-module over F^nr. Finite dimensionality follows because Hom_{G_K}(C,B_st) ↪ Hom_{G_K}(C,B_dR) = 0 by Proposition 2.14(iv), which reduces the question to finite dimensional Q_p-representations. Moreover the natural maps D^*_st(W) ⊗_F K → D^*_dR(W) and (D^*_pst(W) ⊗_{F^nr} K̄)^{G_K} → D^*_dR(W), induced by B_st ⊗_F K ↪ B_dR and B_st ⊗_{F^nr} K̄ ↪ B_dR, are injective.

items.name: Theorem 5.8: D^* of V_st for an acyclic filtered (ϕ,N)-module over K
items.statement: For (M,Fil^•) an acyclic filtered (ϕ,N)-module over K one has D^*_st(V_st(M,Fil^•)) ≅ M^* as (ϕ,N)-modules over F and D^*_dR(V_st(M,Fil^•)) ≅ (M^*_K,Fil^•_⊥) as filtered K-modules — an extension to acyclic modules of a classical result for admissible ones. By Remark 5.5(iv) the natural pairing injects M^* into Hom_{G_K}(V,B_st) and M^*_K into Hom_{G_K}(V,B_dR), and the injectivity of K ⊗_F Hom_{G_K}(V,B_st) → Hom_{G_K}(V,B_dR) reduces everything to the de Rham statement. Picking Fil^•_1 ⊂ Fil^• admissible, the sequence (5.6) reads 0 → V_1 → V → W → 0 with W a sum of t^{k_1}B^+_dR/t^{k_2}B^+_dR, so D^*_dR(W) = 0 by Proposition 2.14 and one gets injections M^*_K ↪ D^*_dR(V) ↪ D^*_dR(V_1); but dim_K D^*_dR(V_1) ≤ dim_{Q_p}V_1 = dim_K M_K because V_1 is de Rham, so these are isomorphisms. For the filtrations: extending µ ∈ M^*_K to a B_dR-linear map, Remark 5.5(iv) makes µ(V) ⊂ t^iB^+_dR equivalent to µ(Fil^0(M_K ⊗ B_dR)) ⊂ t^iB^+_dR, and since Fil^0(M_K ⊗ B_dR) = Σ_n Fil^nM_K ⊗ t^{−n}B^+_dR with µ(M_K) ⊂ K, that holds iff µ(Fil^nM_K) = 0 for n ≥ 1−i, i.e. iff µ ∈ Fil^i_⊥M^*_K.
items.note: The hypothesis is a filtered (ϕ,N)-module, with no G_K-action; Corollary 5.9 gives the equivariant version. One intermediate sentence prints the deduction with the arrow "D^*_st → M^*" reversed — the map constructed is M^* → D^*_st, as the parallel passage in Corollary 5.9 states correctly. Remark 5.22 notes that this method could also prove Propositions 5.18 and 5.20.

items.name: Corollary 5.9: the (ϕ,N,G_K)-version
items.statement: For (M,Fil^•) an acyclic filtered (ϕ,N,G_K)-module over K, D^*_pst(V_st(M,Fil^•)) ≅ M^* as (ϕ,N,G_K)-modules over F^nr and D^*_dR(V_st(M,Fil^•)) ≅ (M^*_K,Fil^•_⊥) as filtered K-modules. As in Theorem 5.8 one has injections of the right-hand sides into the left-hand sides and need only bound the dimensions, which is achieved by passing to a finite L/K over which the action on M is unramified and applying the theorem to a (ϕ,N)-module M(L) over F_L with M = F^nr ⊗_{F_L} M(L).
items.note: The proof says "applying the proposition", where Theorem 5.8 — called "the above theorem" two lines earlier — is meant.

items.name: Corollary 5.10: the Tate-twisted form V^r_st
items.statement: For (M,Fil^•) acyclic over K with ϕ-slopes in [0,r], Fil^0M_K = M_K and Fil^{r+1}M_K = 0, set V^r_st(M,Fil^•) := ker((M ⊗_{F^nr} B^+_st)^{N=0,ϕ=p^r} → (M_K ⊗_K B^+_dR)/Fil^r). Then D^*_pst(V^r_st) ≅ M^*{r} as (ϕ,N,G_K)-modules over F^nr and D^*_dR(V^r_st) ≅ (M^*_K,Fil^•_⊥{r}) as filtered K-modules, where M{r} and Fil^•_⊥{r} mean that ϕ is multiplied by p^r and the filtration shifted by r, Fil^i_⊥{r} = Fil^{i−r}_⊥. The hypotheses give V^r_st(M,Fil^•) = t^rV_st(M,Fil^•), so the Hom's are the t^r-multiples of those of Corollary 5.9.

items.name: Example 5.11: the case Fil^rM_K = M_K
items.statement: If M in Corollary 5.10 satisfies Fil^rM_K = M_K then (M_K ⊗_K B^+_dR)/Fil^r = 0, so V^r_st(M,Fil^•) = X^r_st(M) := (M ⊗_{F^nr} B^+_st)^{N=0,ϕ=p^r}, and the corollary becomes Hom^{sm}_{G_K}(X^r_st(M),B_st) ≅ M^* as (ϕ,N,G_K)-modules over F^nr, and Hom_{G_K}(X^r_st(M),t^jB^+_dR) ≅ M^*_K for j ≤ 0 and 0 for j ≥ 1.
items.note: The second value is printed M_K where the K-dual M^*_K is meant, as the companion line of the same display and the formula quoted in §1.3.2 both show. Under the standing hypotheses Fil^rM_K = M_K forces a single filtration jump, at r.

items.name: Lemma 5.12: no maps from V^r_st to C(j) for j ≥ r+1
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Corollary 5.10, Hom_{G_K}(V^r_st(M,Fil^•),C(j)) = 0 for j ≥ r+1. Writing V := V^r_st as 0 → V_1 → V → W → 0 as in the proof of Theorem 5.8, with V_1 of dimension dim(M), de Rham with Hodge–Tate weights in [0,r], and W a sum of t^aB^+_dR/t^bB^+_dR with 0 ≤ a ≤ b ≤ r+1: Lemma 2.10 gives Hom_{C(G_K)}(W,C(j)) = 0 since j ≥ r+1 ≥ b, and the Hodge–Tate weights of V_1 being ≤ r gives Hom_{C(G_K)}(V_1,C(j)) = 0, so the exact sequence forces the vanishing for V.
items.note: The last displayed vanishing is printed for V rather than for V_1, which is the input the exact sequence needs. Hom_{G_K} and Hom_{C(G_K)} agree by Theorem 2.1 and Proposition 2.5.

items.name: Filtered (ϕ,N)-modules over C and their bundles
items.statement: A filtered (ϕ,N)-module over C is a pair (M,M^+_dR) with M a (ϕ,N)-module over F^nr and M^+_dR ⊂ M ⊗_{F^nr} B_dR a B^+_dR-lattice. To it is attached a vector bundle E(M,M^+_dR) on X_FF characterized by H^0(X_FF ∖ {∞},E) = (M ⊗_{F^nr} B_st)^{N=0,ϕ=1} and E ⊗ Ô_{X_FF,∞} = M^+_dR, and one sets V_st(M,M^+_dR) := H^0(X_FF,E) = ker((M ⊗_{F^nr} B_st)^{N=0,ϕ=1} → (M ⊗_{F^nr} B_dR)/M^+_dR). Compared with the theory over K there is no G_K-action and no filtration on a K-rational M_K: the de Rham datum is the single lattice, so no descent conditions are imposed and no t_N/t_H degree is defined — the slopes are those of the bundle.

items.name: Weakly admissible and acyclic filtered (ϕ,N)-modules over C
items.statement: (M,M^+_dR) is weakly admissible if E(M,M^+_dR) is semistable of slope 0, and acyclic if the slopes of E(M,M^+_dR) are ≥ 0.
items.note: Over C the notions are defined directly on the bundle, so there is no sign ambiguity here; this is what fixes the intended sign in Definition 5.1.

items.name: Remark 5.14: criteria over C
items.statement: (i) If (M,Fil^•) over K is weakly admissible (resp. acyclic), so is the induced (M ⊗_F F^nr, Fil^0(M_K ⊗_K B_dR)) over C. (ii) By the classification of bundles on X_FF, (M,M^+_dR) is weakly admissible if and only if it is admissible, i.e. E is a sum of trivial line bundles — equivalently V_st(M,M^+_dR) is finite dimensional over Q_p and 0 → V_st → (M ⊗ B_st)^{N=0,ϕ=1} → (M ⊗ B_dR)/M^+_dR → 0 is exact; in that case V_st ⊗_{Q_p} B_st → M ⊗_{F^nr} B_st and V_st ⊗_{Q_p} B^+_dR → M^+_dR are isomorphisms. (iii) The following are equivalent: (M,M^+_dR) is acyclic; H^1(X,E(M,M^+_dR)) = 0; (M ⊗ B_st)^{N=0,ϕ=1} → (M ⊗ B_dR)/M^+_dR is surjective; there is a sub-lattice N^+_dR ⊂ M^+_dR with (M,N^+_dR) weakly admissible. The first two are equivalent by Theorem 3.9 and (3.10), the second and third because that H^1 is the cokernel of the displayed map, and the first and last by the argument of Lemma 5.3.
items.note: The last bullet — a weakly admissible lattice contained in M^+_dR — is the form used in Proposition 5.23; the proof of Proposition 5.20 states the opposite inclusion.

items.name: Remark 5.15: acyclicity is stable under tensor product
items.statement: Since (M,M^+_dR) ↦ E(M,M^+_dR) commutes with tensor products and the slope of E ⊗ E′ is the sum of the slopes, the tensor product of two acyclic filtered (ϕ,N)-modules over C is again acyclic.
items.note: Used in the proof of Theorem 8.1(a) for a product of two varieties with de Rham slopes ≥ 0. The printed statement says "filtered ϕ-modules", omitting the N.

items.name: Remark 5.16: acyclicity in the bounded normalisation
items.statement: Assume the ϕ-slopes are in [0,r] and M ⊗ t^rB^+_dR ⊂ t^rM^+_dR ⊂ M ⊗ B^+_dR. Then the following are equivalent: (M,M^+_dR) is acyclic; (M ⊗_{F^nr} B_st)^{N=0,ϕ=p^r} → (M ⊗_{F^nr} B_dR)/t^rM^+_dR is surjective; for all k ≥ 0, (M ⊗ t^{−k}B^+_st)^{N=0,ϕ=p^r} → (M ⊗ t^{−k}B^+_dR)/t^rM^+_dR is surjective. This rests on the isomorphism (M ⊗ t^{−k}B^+_st)^{N=0,ϕ=p^r}/(M ⊗ t^{1−k}B^+_st)^{N=0,ϕ=p^r} ≅ (M ⊗ t^{−k}B^+_dR)/(M ⊗ t^{1−k}B^+_dR) for k ≥ 1, shown by a Dimension argument: there is a natural injection extending to a morphism of BC's of the same Dimension (dim M,0), immediate on the right and, on the left, from the authors' earlier Dimension computations. For the same reasons t^rV_st(M,M^+_dR) = ker((M ⊗ t^{−k}B^+_st)^{N=0,ϕ=p^r} → (M ⊗ t^{−k}B^+_dR)/t^rM^+_dR) for all k ≥ 0.

items.name: Lemma 5.17: the ϕ-eigenspace generates the de Rham lattice
items.statement: For M a (ϕ,N)-module over F^nr with ϕ-slopes in [0,r], the Q_p-module (M ⊗_{F^nr} B^+_st)^{N=0,ϕ=p^r} generates the B^+_dR-module M ⊗_{F^nr} B^+_dR. Since B^+_dR is local with residue field C it suffices to generate M ⊗_{F^nr} C. The map x ↦ x − uNx + (u^2/2!)N^2x − ⋯, for u ∈ B^+_st mapping to log([p^♭]/p), gives a ϕ-equivariant isomorphism M ⊗ B^+_cris ≅ (M ⊗ B^+_st)^{N=0}, and u has image 0 in C, so one reduces to (M ⊗ B^+_cris)^{ϕ=p^r}. Since B^+_cris contains W(k_C), Dieudonné–Manin reduces to M elementary with slope a/h ≤ r, generated by e_1,…,e_h with ϕ(e_i) = e_{i+1} and ϕ(e_h) = p^ae_1; then x ↦ xe_1 + p^{−r}ϕ(x)e_2 + ⋯ + p^{−(h−1)r}ϕ^{h−1}(x)e_h identifies U_{h,rh−a} with (M ⊗ B^+_cris)^{ϕ=p^r}, using r ≥ a/h, and one must show that the image of U_{h,rh−a} under x ↦ (θ(x),…,θ(ϕ^{h−1}(x))) does not lie in a proper sub-C-module of C^h. If it did, applying the relation to αx for α ∈ Q_{p^h} and setting µ_i(x) = λ_iθ(ϕ^i(x)) gives Σ_i µ_i(x)ϕ^i(α) = 0 for all α, and linear independence of characters forces all µ_i = 0.
items.note: §1.3.1 lists this as one of the ingredients of Proposition 7.10 and notes that it is in its application that the restriction to cohomological degrees ≤ r is used in an essential way. §5.4.1 also advertises these results as key arguments in the proof of Theorem 8.1, whereas the §5.4 header and §1.3.2 route them to Proposition 7.10 and Chapter 9.

items.name: Proposition 5.18: the VS-Hom out of X^r_st(M)
items.statement: For M a (ϕ,N)-module with ϕ-slopes in [0,r] and X^r_st(M) := (M ⊗_{F^nr} B^+_st)^{N=0,ϕ=p^r}, one has Hom_VS(X^r_st(M),B_dR) ≅ M^* ⊗_{F^nr} B_dR and Hom_VS(X^r_st(M),B_st) ≅ M^* ⊗_{F^nr} B_st. Indeed X^r_st(M) is of curvature ≤ 0 and the slope conditions give ht(X^r_st(M)) = rk(M), so Proposition 3.27 gives rk(h(X^r_st(M))) = rk(M); the inclusion B^+_st ↪ B_dR induces M^* ⊗ B_dR → h(X^r_st(M)), injective by Lemma 5.17, hence an isomorphism by equality of ranks over B_dR. For the second isomorphism one must show that λ ∈ M^* ⊗ B_dR with λ(X^r_st(M)) ⊂ B_st lies in M^* ⊗ B_st: picking a weakly admissible M^+_dR and V := V_st(M,M^+_dR), so that V ⊗ B_st ≅ M ⊗ B_st, one has t^rV ⊂ X^r_st(M), hence λ(V) ⊂ B_st, and V generates M ⊗ B_st.
items.note: The height computation ht(X^r_st(M)) = rk(M) is quoted from the authors’ earlier paper. This is the categorified companion of Theorem 5.8: Hom_VS is Hom in the category of Vector Spaces, not merely of G_K-equivariant maps. Remark 5.19 adds the crystalline variant X^r_st(M) ≅ X^r_cris(M) := (M ⊗ B^+_cris)^{ϕ=p^r} and the inclusions M^* ⊗ B^+_cris ⊂ Hom_VS(X^r_cris(M),B^+_cris) ⊂ M^* ⊗ t^{−r}B^+_cris.

items.name: Proposition 5.20: the VS-Hom out of V^r_st over C
items.statement: Let (M,M^+_dR) be an acyclic filtered (ϕ,N)-module over C with ϕ-slopes in [0,r] and t^rB^+_dR ⊗ M ⊂ t^rM^+_dR ⊂ B^+_dR ⊗ M, and set V^r_st(M,M^+_dR) := ker((M ⊗_{F^nr} B^+_st)^{N=0,ϕ=p^r} → (M ⊗_{F^nr} B^+_dR)/t^rM^+_dR). Then Hom_VS(V^r_st,B_dR) ≅ M^* ⊗_{F^nr} B_dR and Hom_VS(V^r_st,B_st) ≅ M^* ⊗_{F^nr} B_st. With X^r_dR(M) := (M ⊗ B^+_dR)/t^rM^+_dR, a B^+_dR-module killed by t^r, the hypotheses give the exact sequence 0 → V^r_st → X^r_st(M) → X^r_dR(M) → 0, and the first isomorphism follows from Proposition 5.18 together with the vanishing of Hom_VS(X^r_dR(M),B_dR) and Ext^1_VS(X^r_dR(M),B_dR) by Corollary 3.18 and Lemma 3.26; for the second one picks a weakly admissible lattice N^+_dR ⊂ M^+_dR, which acyclicity provides, sets V := V_st(M,N^+_dR) and argues as in Proposition 5.18. The crystalline variant of Remark 5.19 holds here too.
items.note: Announced in the §5 preamble as the tool for the pro-étale-to-de Rham conjecture over C. Three blemishes in the printed text: the source of V^r_st is written with B_st where B^+_st is needed for the map and the exact sequence to make sense; the Ext^1 carries a natural sign superscript used nowhere else and never defined, Lemma 3.26 giving plain Ext^1_VS; and the weakly admissible lattice is said to contain M^+_dR, where Remark 5.14(iii) and the argument both require it to be contained in M^+_dR.

items.name: Proposition 5.23: the comparison modulo t^k
items.statement: Let (M,M^+_dR) be acyclic over C with ϕ-slopes in [0,r] and M ⊗ t^rB^+_dR ⊂ t^rM^+_dR ⊂ M ⊗ B^+_dR, and let k ≥ 2r. Then the natural map M^* ⊗_{F^nr} (B^+_dR/t^k) → Hom_VS(V^r_st(M,M^+_dR),B^+_dR/t^k) induced by V^r_st ⊂ M ⊗ B^+_dR has kernel and cokernel killed by t^{2r}. Choose N^+_dR with M ⊗ B^+_dR ⊂ N^+_dR ⊂ M^+_dR and (M,N^+_dR) weakly admissible, possible by the adaptation of Lemma 5.4 to (ϕ,N)-modules over C; put V_1 = V^r_st(M,N^+_dR), V = V^r_st(M,M^+_dR) and W = V/V_1, so that V_1 is a finite dimensional Q_p-vector space and W = t^rM^+_dR/t^rN^+_dR is killed by t^r. Writing h_k(−) = Hom_VS(−,B^+_dR/t^k), the chain of inclusions of the four modules between (M ⊗ t^rB^+_dR)/t^k and (M ⊗ B^+_dR)/t^k gives a commutative diagram in which the composite M^* ⊗ (B^+_dR/t^k) → M^* ⊗ (t^rB^+_dR/t^k) is multiplication by t^r; since V_1 is finite dimensional and N^+_dR = V_1 ⊗ t^{−r}B^+_dR, Proposition 3.17 identifies h_k of the N-term with V_1^* ⊗ (B^+_dR/t^k) = h_k(V_1). Hence the kernel of M^* ⊗ (B^+_dR/t^k) → h_k(V) is a subobject of the kernel of multiplication by t^r, so killed by t^r; and since the cokernel of h_k(V) → h_k(V_1) is a subquotient of the cokernel of t^r, and the kernel of that map is h_k(W), also killed by t^r, the cokernel of M^* ⊗ (B^+_dR/t^k) → h_k(V) is killed by t^{2r}.
items.note: The leftmost entry of the printed top row of the diagram reads M^* ⊗ (t^rB^+_dR/t^k), whereas the row is h_k applied to the displayed chain whose largest term has h_k = M^* ⊗ (B^+_dR/t^k), and the sentence below the diagram and both bullet points use that form.

items.name: Proposition 6.1: the cohomologies attached to an analytic variety
items.statement: Quoted from the authors' parts I and companion. (1) To any smooth dagger or rigid analytic variety X over C there are naturally associated: (a) pro-étale cohomology RΓ_proét(X,Q_p(r)) ∈ D(C_{Q_p}) for r ∈ Z; (b) syntomic cohomology RΓ_syn(X,Q_p(r)) for r ∈ N with a period morphism α_r : RΓ_syn(X,Q_p(r)) → RΓ_proét(X,Q_p(r)) that is a strict quasi-isomorphism after τ^{≤r} and lifts to the derived category of topological vector spaces; (c) Hyodo–Kato cohomology RΓ_HK(X) ∈ D_{ϕ,N}(F^nr) with strict quasi-isomorphisms ι_HK : RΓ_HK(X) ⊗̂^R_{F^nr} C ≅ RΓ_dR(X) and ι_HK : RΓ_HK(X) ⊗̂^R_{F^nr} B^+_dR ≅ RΓ_dR(X/B^+_dR); (d) a distinguished triangle RΓ_syn(X,Q_p(r)) → [RΓ_HK(X) ⊗̂_{F^nr} B^+_st]^{N=0,ϕ=p^r} --ι_HK--> RΓ_dR(X/B^+_dR)/F^r, liftable to topological vector spaces; (e) compatibility with the constructions from a semistable weak formal model when one exists. (2) For X smooth dagger with completion X̂ there are natural compatible morphisms ι_proét, ι, and maps on de Rham, B^+_dR- and Hyodo–Kato cohomology from X to X̂, all strict quasi-isomorphisms preserving the extra structures when X is partially proper.
items.note: Quoted wholesale from the authors' part I and its companion; nothing here is proved in this paper. The triangle (1)(d) is the object whose splitting into short exact sequences is the content of the C_st-conjecture.

items.name: Theorem 6.2: the algebraic comparison, after Beilinson
items.statement: For X_K an algebraic variety over K and X = X_{K,K̄}, and r ≥ 0: a natural B_st-linear G_K-equivariant α_st : H^r_ét(X,Q_p) ⊗_{Q_p} B_st ≅ H^r_HK(X) ⊗_{F^nr} B_st preserving ϕ and N, inducing a filtered α_dR : H^r_ét(X,Q_p) ⊗_{Q_p} B_dR ≅ H^r_dR(X_K) ⊗_K B_dR; whence H^r_ét(X,Q_p) ≅ (H^r_HK(X) ⊗_{F^nr} B_st)^{ϕ=1,N=0} ∩ F^0(H^r_dR(X_K) ⊗_K B_dR) as a G_K-module, and (6.3) Hom^sm_{G_K}(H^r_ét(X,Q_p),B_st) ≅ H^r_HK(X)^* as a (ϕ,N,G_K)-module, Hom_{G_K}(H^r_ét(X,Q_p),B_dR) ≅ H^r_dR(X_K)^* as a filtered K-module. There is no hypothesis on the variety.
items.note: Quoted from Beilinson; this formulation is the template for the analytic theorems that follow.

items.name: Theorem 6.4: C_st for proper smooth rigid analytic varieties over K
items.statement: For X_K proper and smooth rigid analytic over K, X = X_{K,C} and r ≥ 0: a natural B_st-linear G_K-equivariant α_st : H^r_ét(X,Q_p) ⊗_{Q_p} B_st ≅ H^r_HK(X) ⊗_{F^nr} B_st preserving ϕ and N, inducing a filtered α_dR : H^r_ét(X,Q_p) ⊗_{Q_p} B_dR ≅ H^r_dR(X_K) ⊗_K B_dR, and hence (6.5) the two Hom-descriptions of H^r_HK(X)^* and H^r_dR(X_K)^*. Finiteness of the groups comes from Scholze for étale cohomology and from the Hyodo–Kato isomorphism for Hyodo–Kato cohomology. The proof runs the syntomic period map for s > r, uses the degeneration of the Hodge–de Rham spectral sequence to get the long exact sequence (6.6), and splits it by the theory of Banach–Colmez spaces: the cokernel of f_r is of Dimension (0,d_r) while the de Rham term is a successive extension of C-vector spaces, so any map from the latter to the former vanishes; a weight argument then gives V_st(H^r_HK(X),H^r_dR(X_K)) ≅ H^r_ét(X,Q_p) and a dimension count gives t_N = t_H, whence weak admissibility.
items.note: Generalises the authors' earlier corollary, where semistable reduction was assumed. The proof is the same Banach-Space Dimension argument as in PAPER-COLMEZ-NIZIOL-17 §5.2.

items.name: Remark 6.7: the Hom-isomorphisms are strict
items.statement: The isomorphisms (6.3) and (6.5) are strict for the natural topologies on the Hom's.

items.name: Theorem 6.8: C_st for smooth proper rigid analytic varieties over C
items.statement: For X smooth proper rigid analytic over C — whose étale cohomology is of finite rank by Scholze, whose Hyodo–Kato cohomology is of finite rank by the Hyodo–Kato isomorphism, and whose B^+_dR-cohomology is free of finite rank — and r ≥ 0: a natural B_st-linear α_st : H^r_ét(X,Q_p) ⊗_{Q_p} B_st ≅ H^r_HK(X) ⊗_{F^nr} B_st preserving ϕ and N, inducing a filtered (6.9) α_dR : H^r_ét(X,Q_p) ⊗_{Q_p} B_dR ≅ H^r_dR(X/B^+_dR) ⊗_{B^+_dR} B_dR, where F^iH^r_dR(X/B^+_dR) := Im(H^r(F^iRΓ_dR(X/B^+_dR)) → H^r_dR(X/B^+_dR)). The proof notes that H^r(RΓ_dR(X/B^+_dR)/F^s) is a Banach–Colmez space, a successive extension of finite-rank C-vector spaces, obtains the short exact sequence (6.11) 0 → H^r_ét(X,Q_p(s)) → (H^r_HK(X) ⊗_{F^nr} B^+_st)^{N=0,ϕ=p^s} → H^r(RΓ_dR(X/B^+_dR)/F^s) → 0, shows that H^r_dR(X/B^+_dR)/F^s → H^r(RΓ_dR(X/B^+_dR)/F^s) is an isomorphism, and concludes from the acyclicity criteria for filtered (ϕ,N)-modules over C.
items.note: An unfiltered de Rham comparison of this shape was constructed earlier by Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze; Remark 6.10 records that the filtered statement is the new content.

items.name: Remark 6.13: the Fargues–Fontaine and Hom restatements
items.statement: (i) Theorem 6.8 can be restated as H^r_ét(X,Q_p) ≅ H^0(X_FF, E(H^r_HK(X), F^0H^r_dR(X/B_dR))), where E(−,−) is the vector bundle on the Fargues–Fontaine curve attached to a filtered (ϕ,N)-module over C. (ii) It gives Hom_VS(H^r_ét(X,Q_p),B_st) ≅ Hom_{F^nr}(H^r_HK(X),B_st) as B_st-modules and Hom_VS(H^r_ét(X,Q_p),B_dR) ≅ Hom_{B^+_dR}(H^r_dR(X/B^+_dR),B_dR) as B_dR-modules — that is, Conjecture 1.8 in the proper case.

items.name: Theorem 6.14: the simplified fundamental diagram for dagger Stein and affinoid
items.statement: For X a smooth dagger Stein variety or a smooth dagger affinoid over C and r ≥ 0, there is a natural map of strictly exact sequences in D(C_{Q_p}) from 0 → Ω^{r−1}(X)/ker d → H^r_proét(X,Q_p(r)) → (H^r_HK(X) ⊗̂_{F^nr} B^+_st)^{N=0,ϕ=p^r} → 0 to 0 → Ω^{r−1}(X)/ker d --d--> Ω^r(X)^{d=0} → H^r_dR(X) → 0, with identity on the left, β̃ in the middle and ι_HK ⊗ θ on the right. Moreover H^r_proét(X,Q_p(r)) is Fréchet in the Stein case and LB in the affinoid case, the vertical maps are strict with closed images, and ker β̃ ≅ (H^r_HK(X) ⊗̂_{F^nr} B^+_st)^{N=0,ϕ=p^{r−1}}. The map is β̃ := p^{−r}βα_r^{−1}, the twist by p^{−r} making it compatible with symbols.
items.note: Deduced from part I's fundamental diagram for overconvergent syntomic cohomology; it generalises PAPER-COLMEZ-DOSPINESCU-NIZIOL-20's Theorem 1.8, which assumed a semistable model.

items.name: Corollary 6.15: the bicartesian square in the proper case
items.statement: For X smooth proper rigid analytic over C the square with corners H^r_ét(X,Q_p(r)), (H^r_HK(X) ⊗_{F^nr} B^+_st)^{ϕ=p^r,N=0}, F^rH^r_dR(X/B^+_dR) and H^r_dR(X/B^+_dR), with maps α_st(r), α_dR(r), ι_HK ⊗ ι and the canonical map, is bicartesian — equivalently (6.17) 0 → H^r_ét(X,Q_p(r)) → (H^r_HK ⊗ B^+_st)^{N=0,ϕ=p^r} ⊕ F^rH^r_dR(X/B^+_dR) → H^r_dR(X/B^+_dR) → 0 is exact. It follows from the short exact sequence (6.11), and the passage back from the diagram to Theorem 6.8 is also possible; moreover H^r(F^rRΓ_dR(X/B^+_dR)) → F^rH^r_dR(X/B^+_dR) is an isomorphism in this case (Remark 6.18).
items.note: In the proper case both horizontal arrows are injective.

items.name: Corollary 6.19: the bicartesian square for dagger Stein and affinoid
items.statement: For X a smooth dagger Stein variety or a smooth dagger affinoid over C and r ≥ 0, the square with corners H^r_proét(X,Q_p(r)), (H^r_HK(X) ⊗̂_{F^nr} B^+_st)^{N=0,ϕ=p^r}, H^r(F^rRΓ_dR(X/B^+_dR)) and H^r_dR(X/B^+_dR) is bicartesian in D(C_{Q_p}), all the cohomologies being classical. The proof compares the two distinguished triangles — the syntomic one and the Hodge-filtration one — notes that H^i(RΓ_dR(X/B^+_dR)/F^r) = 0 for i ≥ r so that both maps are surjective in degrees ≥ r, and identifies the two kernels in degree r, both being (Ω^{r−1}(X)/ker d) ⊗̂ C.
items.note: Here both horizontal arrows are surjective with kernel Ω^{r−1}(X)/ker d. The statement is printed with H^r_ét where H^r_proét is meant (source issue).

items.name: The fundamental diagram
items.statement: For X a smooth dagger variety over C and i ≤ r, the fundamental diagram is the commutative square with top-left H^i_proét(X,Q_p(r)), top-right the Hyodo–Kato term (H^i_HK(X) ⊗̂_{F^nr} B^+_st)^{N=0,ϕ=p^r}, bottom-left H^i(F^rRΓ_dR(X/B^+_dR)) and bottom-right H^i_dR(X/B^+_dR); the top map is the period map α_st(r) coming from the comparison with syntomic cohomology and the triangle of Proposition 6.1(1)(d), the left map is α_dR(r), the right map is ι_HK ⊗ ι, and the bottom map is canonical. Its assertion is bicartesianness, equivalently the exactness of 0 → H^i_proét(X,Q_p(r)) → (H^i_HK ⊗̂ B^+_st)^{N=0,ϕ=p^r} ⊕ H^i(F^rRΓ_dR(X/B^+_dR)) → H^i_dR(X/B^+_dR) → 0. In the proper case the bottom-left corner agrees with F^iH^r_dR(X/B^+_dR).

items.name: Conjecture 6.21: the C_st-conjecture
items.statement: For X a smooth dagger variety over C and r ≥ i, the fundamental diagram with the left-heart cohomology objects H̃^i is bicartesian; equivalently (6.22) 0 → H̃^i_proét(X,Q_p(r)) → (H̃^i_HK(X) ⊗̂_{F^nr} B^+_st)^{N=0,ϕ=p^r} ⊕ H̃^iF^rRΓ_dR(X/B^+_dR) → H̃^i_dR(X/B^+_dR) → 0 is exact in the left heart LH(C_{Q_p}) of the derived category of the quasi-abelian category of convex Q_p-vector spaces. No properness, quasi-compactness or model hypothesis; the only restriction is on the degree, i ≤ r.
items.note: This is Conjecture 1.4 of the introduction. The degree restriction enters through Lemma 5.17, because i ≤ r makes the slopes of Frobenius on Hyodo–Kato cohomology ≤ r.

items.name: Remark 6.23: known cases, twist invariance, reduction to surjectivity
items.statement: (i) The conjecture is known for X proper, where both horizontal arrows are injective, and for X Stein or affinoid, where both are surjective with kernel Ω^{r−1}(X)/ker d. (ii) With H̃^{r,i} := H̃^i_proét(X,Q_p(r)), X̃^{r,i} := (H̃^i_HK ⊗̂ B^+_st)^{N=0,ϕ=p^r}, F̃^{r,i} := H̃^i(F^rRΓ_dR(X/B^+_dR)) and B̃^i := H̃^i_dR(X/B^+_dR) — the X̃ and B̃ being classical — there is a commutative diagram with exact rows and columns whose vertical maps are multiplication by t (the Tate twist on pro-étale cohomology), using X^{r+1,i}/tX^{r,i} ≅ H^i_HK(X) ⊗̂_{F^nr} C, the identity τ^{≤i}F^{r+1}RΓ_dR(X/B^+_dR) = tF^rRΓ_dR(X/B^+_dR) valid because i ≤ r, and the Hyodo–Kato map; it follows that for fixed i the conjecture for r is equivalent to the conjecture for r+1, so it suffices to prove it for one r ≥ i. (iii) Since the B̃^i are classical and there is a long exact sequence, induction on i reduces the conjecture to the surjectivity of X^{r,i} ⊕ F^{r,i} → B^i. (iv) It is proved for many small varieties in Theorem 8.1.
items.note: (ii) and (iii) are the two structural reductions the whole of §7 rests on.

items.name: The filtration conventions on B^+_dR-cohomology
items.statement: For X a smooth dagger variety over C: F^iH^r_dR(X/B^+_dR) := Im(H^r(F^iRΓ_dR(X/B^+_dR)) → H^r_dR(X/B^+_dR)), and H^r_dR(X/B_dR) := H^r_dR(X/B^+_dR) ⊗̂_{B^+_dR} B_dR with the induced filtration.
items.note: These conventions make F^0H^r_dR(X/B_dR) a B^+_dR-lattice, so that (H^r_HK(X),F^0H^r_dR(X/B_dR)) is a filtered (ϕ,N)-module over C.

items.name: Conjecture 7.1: acyclicity of de Rham cohomology
items.statement: For X a smooth quasi-compact dagger variety over C and all r, the map (H^r_HK(X) ⊗̂_{F^nr} B^+_st)^{N=0,ϕ=p^r} → H^r_dR(X/B^+_dR)/F^r is surjective — equivalently the filtered (ϕ,N)-module (H^r_HK(X),F^0H^r_dR(X/B_dR)) is acyclic, that is the slopes of the associated bundle on the Fargues–Fontaine curve are ≥ 0, equivalently its H^1 vanishes, equivalently it admits a sub-lattice making it weakly admissible.
items.note: A smooth dagger variety is said to have de Rham slopes ≥ 0 when it is small and satisfies this conjecture for all r ≥ 0. Remark 7.2: proper varieties satisfy it because the pair is weakly admissible, and affinoids because the target vanishes.

items.name: Conjecture 7.3: pro-étale cohomology has curvature ≤ 0
items.statement: For X a smooth quasi-compact dagger variety over C, H^r_proét(X,Q_p) — which is naturally a qBC by Corollary 7.9 — has curvature ≤ 0 for all r ≥ 0, that is its curvature-positive part W_{>0} vanishes.

items.name: Conjecture 7.4: the height equals the de Rham dimension
items.statement: For X a smooth quasi-compact dagger variety over C and all r, ht(H^r_proét(X,Q_p)) = dim_C H^r_dR(X), the height of a qBC being ht(W) = ht(W_{>0}) + ht(W_{<0}).
items.note: The analytic analogue of dim_{Q_p}H^i_ét = dim_K H^i_dR. Remark 7.5(i) proves it for X proper, from the short exact sequence (6.11) together with the facts that the Frobenius slopes on H^r_HK are ≤ r and that a finite dimensional Q_p-space has height equal to its dimension; Remark 7.5(ii) asks whether a non-proper dagger variety can have finite dimensional pro-étale cohomology in all degrees, noting that already r = 1 with X connected forces O(X) = C.

items.name: Small varieties, in the form §7.2 uses
items.statement: X is small if H^i_dR(X/B^+_dR) is free of finite rank over B^+_dR for all i — for instance X quasi-compact, a naive interior of a quasi-compact, or the analytification of an algebraic variety. Conjectures 6.21, 7.1, 7.3 and 7.4 all make sense in this slightly more general setting.

items.name: Corollary 7.9: pro-étale cohomology is a qBC, with its canonical filtration
items.statement: For X small: (i) H^{r,i} := H^i_proét(X,Q_p(r)) is a qBC, with (H^{r,i})_{>0} ≅ h^1(H^{i−1}_HK{−r}), (H^{r,i})_{<0} ≅ h^0(H^i_HK{−r}) and (H^{r,i})_{=0} ≅ ker(F^{r,i} → B^i), the B^+_dR-torsion of F^{r,i}; (ii) there is an exact sequence 0 → h^1(H^{i−1}_HK{−r}) → H^{r,i} → F^{r,i} ⊕ X^{r,i} → B^i → h^1(H^i_HK{−r}) → 0. Here h^n(H^i_HK{−r}) := H^n(X_FF, E(H^i_HK(X){−r}, F^rH^i_dR(X/B_dR))). The proof reads the three successive quotients off the key diagram: the first is the H^1 of a bundle on the curve, hence a BC of curvature > 0; the last is a sub-BC of a BC of curvature < 0; the middle is a B^+_dR-pair.
items.note: This is what makes Conjectures 7.3 and 7.4 meaningful, and sequence (ii) is the sequence (6.22) of the C_st-conjecture with its two failure terms exhibited.

items.name: The key diagram and the notation of §7.2
items.statement: Fix r and, for i ≤ r, set H^{r,i} := H^i_proét(X,Q_p(r)), X^{r,i} := (H^i_HK(X) ⊗̂_{F^nr} B^+_st)^{N=0,ϕ=p^r}, F^{r,i} := H^i(F^rRΓ_dR(X/B^+_dR)), DR^{r,i} := H^i(RΓ_dR(X/B^+_dR)/F^r), B^i := H^i_dR(X/B^+_dR) and Fil^{r,i} := Im(F^{r,i} → B^i). The isomorphism between pro-étale and syntomic cohomology gives a commutative diagram with three exact rows — the syntomic long exact sequence, the Hodge-filtration long exact sequence and their t^r-reduction — in which (7.6) ker(F^{r,i} → F^{r,i}/t^r) ≅ ker(B^i → B^i/t^rFil^{r,i}), because multiplying by t^r kills the B^+_dR-torsion of F^{r,i} while B^i is free of finite rank by the Hyodo–Kato isomorphism. All the spaces are C-points of topological vector spaces, those in the top and bottom rows of qBC's, and the diagram lifts to topological vector spaces. Lemma 7.7 then identifies h^0(H^i_HK{−r}) with ker(X^{r,i} ⊕ Fil^{r,i} → B^i) ≅ ker(X^{r,i} → B^i/Fil^{r,i}), h^1(H^i_HK{−r}) with the corresponding cokernels, and ker(H^{r,i} → X^{r,i} ⊕ F^{r,i}) with h^1(H^{i−1}_HK{−r}), by the snake lemma applied to (7.8).

items.name: Proposition 7.10: five equivalent properties
items.statement: For X small, the following are equivalent: (a) the diagram of Conjecture 6.21 is bicartesian; (b) h^1(H^i_HK{−r}) = 0 for i = r−1 and i = r; (c) (H^i_HK(X),F^0H^i_dR(X/B_dR)) is acyclic for i = r−1 and i = r; (d) H^{r,r} and H^{r,r+1} have curvature ≤ 0, the second read as syntomic cohomology since it is outside the range of the comparison; (e) ht(H^{r,r}) = dim_C H^r_dR(X). The equivalences (a)⇔(b) and (b)⇔(d) come from Corollary 7.9(ii), (b)⇔(c) is the invariance of acyclicity under twist, and (b)⇔(e) follows from the Euler–Poincaré formula together with ht(h^1(H^i_HK{−r})) < 0 whenever that H^1 is nonzero.
items.note: This is Proposition 1.17 of the introduction, in the form the proofs use.

items.name: Corollary 7.11 and Remark 7.12: the four conjectures are equivalent
items.statement: For X quasi-compact, Conjectures 6.21, 7.1, 7.3 and 7.4 are equivalent; and the same holds more generally for X small, by the same proof. The bookkeeping matters: 6.21 ⇔ 7.4 already for a fixed r, the equivalence with 7.1 requires varying r, and the equivalence with 7.3 uses the twist invariance of Remark 6.23(ii) to return to the range i ≤ r where syntomic and pro-étale cohomology agree.

items.name: Lemma 7.13: the crystalline eigenspace splits
items.statement: For X a quasi-compact dagger variety over C and r ≥ dim X: (i) H^i([RΓ_cris(X)]^{ϕ=p^r}) ≅ (H^i_HK(X) ⊗ B^+_st)^{N=0,ϕ=p^r} as Banach–Colmez spaces; (ii) [RΓ_cris(X)]^{ϕ=p^r} is quasi-isomorphic to the direct sum of its cohomology groups. Part (i) is quoted from part I; part (ii) is proved by writing H^i_HK(X) ≅ ⊕_{j∈J_i}D_j with D_j irreducible of slope a_j/h_j ≤ inf(i,dim X) by Dieudonné–Manin, computing (D_j ⊗ B^+_cris)^{ϕ=p^r} ≅ U_{h_j,rh_j−a_j}e_j — which uses r ≥ dim X — lifting e_j to a cycle ẽ_j and checking that the resulting map of complexes has all arrows zero.

items.name: Proposition 7.15: the canonical filtration splits for r ≥ dim X
items.statement: For r ≥ dim X there is a decomposition H^i_syn(X,r) ≅ h^1(H^{i−1}_HK{−r}) ⊕ h^0(H^i_HK{−r}) ⊕ (Y^{i−1},Z^i) with (Y^{i−1},Z^i) a reasonable B^+_dR-pair: the canonical qBC filtration of Corollary 7.9 splits, non-canonically. The proof writes syntomic cohomology as the fibre of [RΓ_cris(X)]^{ϕ=p^r} ⊕ F^rRΓ_dR(X/B^+_dR) → RΓ_dR(X/B^+_dR), replaces the first term by the sum of its cohomology using Lemma 7.13, reduces to the complex (7.16), splits RΓ^{i−1}_dR/Im d B^+_dR-linearly using that H^{i−1}_dR is free of finite rank and that the spaces are of compact type hence reflexive (with the open mapping theorem), and finally replaces the pair (Ŷ^{i−1},Ẑ^i) by its quotient modulo t^r.
items.note: The authors note this is not used later, and connect it to the open question whether the filtration on every qBC splits.

items.name: Strategy of §8: proving the C_st-conjecture in cases
items.statement: Using Corollary 7.11 the authors prove Conjecture 6.21 first for some quasi-compact smooth dagger varieties and then, by a limit argument, for a product of a smooth proper and a smooth Stein variety. This is the direction in which pro-étale cohomology is reconstructed from Hyodo–Kato and filtered B^+_dR-de Rham data.

items.name: Has de Rham slopes ≥ 0
items.statement: A smooth dagger variety has de Rham slopes ≥ 0 if it is small and satisfies Conjecture 7.1 for all r ≥ 0 — equivalently, if H^i_dR(X/B^+_dR) is free of finite rank over B^+_dR for all i and each filtered (ϕ,N)-module (H^i_HK(X),F^0H^i_dR(X/B_dR)) is acyclic, that is the associated bundle on the Fargues–Fontaine curve has all Harder–Narasimhan slopes ≥ 0. By Corollary 7.11 (and Remark 7.12 for the small rather than quasi-compact case) this implies Conjectures 6.21, 7.3 and 7.4.
items.note: Smallness is part of the definition, so every later "with de Rham slopes ≥ 0" silently assumes the freeness of B^+_dR-cohomology.

items.name: Theorem 8.1: three classes of varieties with de Rham slopes ≥ 0
items.statement: Let X be a smooth dagger variety over C of one of the following (non mutually exclusive) forms: (a) a product of two varieties with de Rham slopes ≥ 0; (b) the analytification of an algebraic variety; (c) an almost proper smooth variety, i.e. the complement in a proper smooth rigid analytic variety of a closed subvariety. Then X has de Rham slopes ≥ 0 — hence satisfies Conjectures 6.21, 7.3 and 7.4. Proof of (a): the Hyodo–Kato and de Rham cup products give a pairing M^i(X) ⊗ M^j(Y) → M^{i+j}(X×Y) of filtered (ϕ,N)-modules; Künneth for Hyodo–Kato cohomology (reduced to de Rham Künneth through the Hyodo–Kato quasi-isomorphism) makes ⊕_{i+j=n}E(M^i(X)) ⊗_O E(M^j(Y)) → E(M^n(X×Y)) an injection with cokernel supported at ∞, and since H^1 of a sheaf supported at ∞ vanishes and a tensor product of acyclic bundles is acyclic (Remark 5.15), H^1(X_FF,E(M^n(X×Y))) = 0. Proof of (b): the filtered (ϕ,N)-module of a smooth algebraic variety is admissible by Beilinson, hence acyclic; Hyodo–Kato GAGA makes M^i(X) → M^i(X^an) an isomorphism on the first factor, so again the cokernel of E(M^i(X)) → E(M^i(X^an)) is supported at ∞ and H^1 vanishes. Proof of (c): by resolution of singularities one may assume Z = D is a simple normal crossings divisor; the exact sequence for the log-space X^× with its logarithmic filtration maps to the sequence for U = X∖D with isomorphisms on the two de Rham terms, which forces f_{i,2} to be surjective for all i ≤ r and hence, by Remark 6.23(iii), f_{i,1} to be injective.
items.note: This is Theorem 1.11/1.12 of the introduction. Admissibility in (b) is quoted from Beilinson; Hyodo–Kato GAGA and the exactness of the log-space sequence in (c) are quoted from Shao, the semistable case being the authors’ earlier work.

items.name: Remark 8.2: étale versus pro-étale for almost proper varieties
items.statement: The proof of Theorem 8.1(c) shows that for U almost proper over C the difference between étale and pro-étale cohomology is the difference between the Hodge filtration and the naive Hodge filtration: [H^i_ét(U,Q_p(r)) → H̃^i_proét(U,Q_p(r))] ≅ [H^i(F^rRΓ(X^×/B^+_dR)) → H̃^i(F^rRΓ(U/B^+_dR))] for i ≤ r, where [C → C'] = holim(C → C' ← 0).

items.name: Proposition 8.3: Grosse-Klönne — the tube and the complement agree
items.statement: Quoted from Grosse-Klönne. (1) Let ϖ ∈ O_K be a uniformizer and Z ↪ 𝔛 a closed immersion of weak formal O_K-schemes such that locally on 𝔛 there are étale morphisms q : 𝔛 → Spf(O_K{X_1,…,X_n}/(X_1⋯X_r − ϖ)) with Z = ∩_{j=r+1}^m V(q^*X_j), for some 1 ≤ r ≤ m ≤ n. Then RΓ_dR(𝔛_K ∖ Z_K) → RΓ_dR(]𝔛_k ∖ Z_k[_𝔛) is a filtered quasi-isomorphism. (2) The same holds with Z = ∪_{j=r+1}^m V(q^*X_j).
items.note: Quoted verbatim from Grosse-Klönne, "De Rham cohomology of rigid spaces"; ]𝔛_k ∖ Z_k[_𝔛 is the open tube of the complement in the special fibre.

items.name: First example: the tube complement in a proper semistable model
items.statement: In the setting of Proposition 8.3 with 𝔛_K proper, U := ]𝔛_k ∖ Z_k[_𝔛 is quasi-compact and U_C has de Rham slopes ≥ 0: via the Hyodo–Kato isomorphism and Proposition 8.3 the canonical map RΓ_HK(𝔛_K ∖ Z_K) → RΓ_HK(U) is a quasi-isomorphism and the analogous map on B_dR-cohomology a filtered quasi-isomorphism, so Theorem 8.1(c) for the left side transfers the property to the right. The authors remark that it should be possible to generalise the two examples of §8.1.1 vastly, but that this would require techniques other than the ones used in the paper.

items.name: Proposition 8.4: removing a small tubular neighbourhood in projective space
items.statement: Let X be a projective space over K and Z a smooth scheme-theoretic intersection Z_1 ×_X ⋯ ×_X Z_c of c hypersurfaces. Then there is ε_0 ∈ |K^*| such that for every ε < ε_0 the canonical morphisms RΓ_dR(X∖Z) → RΓ_dR(X∖Z(ε)) and RΓ_HK(X_C∖Z_C) → RΓ_HK(X_C∖Z(ε)_C) are quasi-isomorphisms compatible with all the structures, where Z(ε) is the tubular neighbourhood of Scholze and of Binda–Kato–Vezzani; similarly with Z replaced by the union of the Z_i. The Hyodo–Kato case follows from the de Rham case by the Hyodo–Kato isomorphism, and the de Rham case from the local product decomposition Z(ε) ≅ Z ×_K B(ε)^c together with Grosse-Klönne's vanishing, the union case by Čech analytic descent. Consequently U(ε)_C := X_C ∖ Z(ε)_C has de Rham slopes ≥ 0, by Theorem 8.1(c).
items.note: The second example, which needs no semistable model but removes a sufficiently small tubular neighbourhood. In the printed proof the local product is written with an undefined symbol Y in place of Z.

items.name: The limit set-up (8.5)–(8.8) for a quasi-compact exhaustion
items.statement: For X a smooth dagger variety over C choose a covering {X_n}_{n∈N} by increasing quasi-compact dagger subvarieties. Set X^{r,i} := (H^i_HK(X) ⊗̂^R_{F^nr} B^+_st)^{N=0,ϕ=p^r}, F^{r,i} := H^i(F^rRΓ_dR(X/B^+_dR)), A^{r,i} := ker(F^{r,i} → H^i_dR(X/B^+_dR)) and F̄^{r,i} := F^{r,i}/A^{r,i}, with the same definitions for each X_n; then F̄^{r,i} ≅ F^rH^i_dR(X/B^+_dR) and F̄^{0,i} ≅ H^i_dR(X/B^+_dR). The goal (8.7) is the exactness of 0 → H^{r,i} → X^{r,i} ⊕ F^{r,i} → F̄^{0,i} → 0, given the exactness (8.8) of 0 → H^{r,i}_n → X^{r,i}_n ⊕ F^{r,i}_n → F̄^{0,i}_n → 0 for every n; so what must be controlled are the various R^1lim_n.
items.note: H^{r,i} and H^{r,i}_n are the pro-étale groups of X and X_n. The printed (8.7) carries a stray subscript n on its F-term.

items.name: Remark 8.9: which R^1lim vanish, and the limit sequence
items.statement: (i) R^1lim_n X^{r,i}_n = 0 and R^1lim_n F̄^{r,i}_n = 0, quoted from part I; the second is proved there for r = 0 and follows in general because F̄^{r,i}_n contains t^rF̄^{0,i}_n with BC quotient. (ii) There are exact sequences 0 → R^1lim_n F^{r,i−1}_n → F^{r,i} → lim_n F^{r,i}_n → 0 and 0 → R^1lim_n H^{r,i−1}_n → H^{r,i} → lim_n H^{r,i}_n → 0, and isomorphisms X^{r,i} ≅ lim_n X^{r,i}_n, F̄^{0,i} ≅ lim_n F̄^{0,i}_n. (iii) Applying lim_n to the sequences (8.8) gives 0 → lim_nH^{r,i}_n → lim_nX^{r,i}_n ⊕ lim_nF^{r,i}_n → lim_nF̄^{0,i}_n → R^1lim_nH^{r,i}_n → R^1lim_nF^{r,i}_n → 0; hence if R^1lim_n H^{r,i}_n = 0 for all i then H^{r,i} ≅ lim_n H^{r,i}_n, (8.7) is exact, and as a bonus R^1lim_n F^{r,i}_n = 0 and F^{r,i} ≅ lim_n F^{r,i}_n. Proving the vanishing for pro-étale cohomology directly is unpromising, so the authors look for statements about the filtered de Rham complexes that imply it, writing DR^{r,i} := H^i(RΓ_dR(X/B^+_dR)/F^r).
items.note: (iii) is printed as "applying lim_n to (6.11)", but (6.11) is the proper-case sequence with no tower index; the sequence being passed to the limit is (8.8).

items.name: Lemma 8.10: DR ⟹ A ⟹ H for the vanishing of R^1lim
items.statement: R^1lim_n DR^{r,i−1}_n = 0 implies R^1lim_n A^{r,i}_n = 0, which implies R^1lim_n H^{r,i}_n = 0. The first implication holds because the long exact sequence ⋯ F̄^{0,i−1}_n → DR^{r,i−1}_n → F^{r,i}_n → F̄^{0,i}_n ⋯ exhibits A^{r,i}_n as a quotient of DR^{r,i−1}_n. For the second, A^{r,i}_n is a subspace of H^{r,i}_n with quotient H̄^{r,i}_n, and the exact sequence 0 → H̄^{r,i}_n → X^{r,i}_n ⊕ (F̄^{r,i}_n/t^rF̄^{0,i}_n) → F̄^{0,i}_n/t^rF̄^{0,i}_n → 0 has all terms but H̄^{r,i}_n a BC, so H̄^{r,i}_n is one too and R^1lim_n H̄^{r,i}_n = 0 by Remark 3.15; the six-term lim/R^1lim sequence then gives the claim.
items.note: Footnote 22 records that (8.8) lifts to Vector Spaces by part I §7.3 and that finite dimensionality of H^i_dR(X_n) makes every term a BC. Remark 8.11 adds that the same proof gives R^1lim_n H̄^{r,i}_n = 0.

items.name: The proper-times-Stein setting
items.statement: Let X := Y ×_C S with Y and S smooth dagger varieties over C, Y proper and S Stein; cover S by a strictly increasing admissible covering {S_n} by open dagger affinoids and set X_n := Y ×_C S_n. Each X_n is a product of a proper and an affinoid dagger variety, hence has de Rham slopes ≥ 0 by Theorem 8.1(a), while X itself is neither quasi-compact nor small in general — which is what the limit machinery of §8.2.1 is for.

items.name: Proposition 8.12: the R^1lim of pro-étale cohomology vanishes
items.statement: For i ≥ 0, R^1lim_n H^i_proét(X_n,Q_p) = 0. Since Rlim_n H^i_proét(X_n,Q_p) = Rlim_n H^i_proét(X̂_n,Q_p) one may pass to the completions, and since the Ŝ_n are quasi-compact one may pass to étale cohomology; Lemma 8.13 and Theorem 6.14 then give R^1lim_n H^i_ét(X_n,Q_p) ≅ ⊕_{j≥0}H^j_ét(Y,Q_p) ⊗_{Q_p} R^1lim_n H^{i−j}_ét(Ŝ_n,Q_p) = 0.

items.name: Lemma 8.13: Künneth for a proper factor
items.statement: For Y, T smooth rigid analytic varieties over C with Y proper and i ≥ 0 there is a Künneth isomorphism (8.14) ⊕_{j≥0}H^j_ét(Y,Q_p) ⊗_{Q_p} H^{i−j}_ét(T,Q_p) ≅ H^i_ét(Y ×_C T,Q_p). Step 1, the integral Künneth formula: RΓ_ét(Y,Z_p) ⊗^L_{Z_p} RΓ_ét(T,Z_p) → RΓ_ét(Y ×_C T,Z_p) is a quasi-isomorphism, the Stacks Project argument going through once one has (8.15) Rp_{2,*}Z_p ≅ RΓ_ét(Y,Z_p) for p_2 : Y ×_C T → T, which is the proper base change theorem of Bhatt–Hansen; applying RΓ_ét(T,−) and using that RΓ_ét(Y,Z_p) is perfect gives RΓ_ét(T,RΓ_ét(Y,Z_p)) ≅ RΓ_ét(T,Z_p) ⊗^L_{Z_p} RΓ_ét(Y,Z_p). Step 2 passes to Q_p-coefficients using perfectness of RΓ_ét(Y,Q_p).
items.note: Proper base change is quoted from Bhatt–Hansen and the Künneth argument from the Stacks Project. In Step 1 the perfectness is printed of RΓ_ét(T,RΓ_ét(Y,Z_p)) rather than of RΓ_ét(Y,Z_p), and the conclusion refers to "the proposition" although 8.13 is a Lemma.

items.name: Remark 8.16: the pro-étale cohomology of a proper times Stein variety
items.statement: (i) Proposition 8.12 gives H^i_proét(X,Q_p) ≅ lim_n H^i_ét(X_n,Q_p). (ii) Its proof also gives the Künneth isomorphism ⊕_{j≥0}H^j_proét(Y,Q_p) ⊗_{Q_p} H^{i−j}_proét(S,Q_p) ≅ H^i_proét(X,Q_p). This decomposition holds only because the cohomology of one factor is finite dimensional: without that assumption it already fails when both factors are the open unit ball of dimension 1.

items.name: Proposition 8.17: the C_st-conjecture for proper times Stein
items.statement: Conjecture 6.21 holds for X = Y ×_C S with Y smooth proper and S smooth Stein over C. For i ≤ r one reduces by Remark 6.23 to the exactness of the sequence of classical cohomologies 0 → H^i_proét(X,Q_p(r)) → (H^i_HK(X) ⊗̂_{F^nr} B^+_st)^{N=0,ϕ=p^r} ⊕ H^iF^rRΓ_dR(X/B^+_dR) → H^i_dR(X/B^+_dR) → 0, and granting Proposition 8.12 this follows from Remark 8.9(iii) together with §8.1.
items.note: This is the case that genuinely needs the limit argument: X is not quasi-compact, and for S Stein H^i_dR(X/B^+_dR) is a Fréchet of infinite rank, so X is not small.

items.name: Strategy of §9: extracting de Rham data from pro-étale cohomology
items.statement: The authors propose a recipe to extract, from the pro-étale cohomology of varieties defined over C, the Hyodo–Kato and de Rham cohomologies as modules over the relevant rings and, for varieties defined over K, to extract also Frobenius, monodromy and the naive Hodge filtration. Over K the extraction is by G_K-equivariant (resp. smooth-G_K) Hom's into B_dR (resp. B_st), which retains ϕ, N and the filtration; over C there is no Galois action and those structures are lost. In both cases the input is Conjecture 6.21, so §9 is §8 plus the vanishing results for Hom's out of torsion B^+_dR-objects.

items.name: Conjecture 9.1: the pro-étale-to-de Rham C_st-conjecture over K
items.statement: For X a smooth dagger variety over K there are natural strict isomorphisms Hom^{sm}_{G_K}(H^i_proét(X_C,Q_p),B_st) ≅ H^i_HK(X_C)^* as a (ϕ,N,G_K)-module and Hom_{G_K}(H^i_proét(X_C,Q_p),B_dR) ≅ H^i_dR(X)^* as a filtered K-module. This extends Fontaine's C_st-conjecture to p-adic analytic spaces. Strictness, in the quasi-abelian category C_K, is part of the claim.
items.note: This is Conjecture 1.6 of the introduction. Remark 9.2 records the equivalent twisted form used in the proofs, with H^i_proét(X_C,Q_p(r)) on the left and M^*{r} on the right, because syntomic cohomology only describes the twisted groups for r ≥ i.

items.name: Theorem 9.3: Conjecture 9.1 for varieties with de Rham slopes ≥ 0
items.statement: Conjecture 9.1 holds for smooth dagger varieties over K with de Rham slopes ≥ 0. The proof occupies §9.1.1 for dagger affinoids, §9.1.2 for quasi-compact varieties and §9.1.3 for the remaining small ones.
items.note: With Theorem 8.1 this is the "over K" half of Theorem 1.11.

items.name: The affinoid case of Theorem 9.3
items.statement: The affinoid case is contained in the quasi-compact one but is considerably simpler; it suffices to produce natural isomorphisms, since the weak topology on the Hom-spaces is Hausdorff. Put M := H^i_HK(X_C), X^i_st(M) := (M ⊗̂^R_{F^nr} B^+_st)^{N=0,ϕ=p^i} and M_K = (K̄ ⊗_{F^nr} M)^{G_K} ≅ H^i_dR(X), the last isomorphism being the Hyodo–Kato isomorphism of part I. Applying Hom^{sm}_{G_K}(−,B_st) and Hom_{G_K}(−,B_dR) to the sequence (9.4) 0 → (Ω^{i−1}_X/ker d) ⊗̂_K C → H^i_proét(X_C,Q_p(i)) → X^i_st(M) → 0 of Theorem 6.14, and killing the outer terms by Lemma 9.5, identifies the Hom's out of pro-étale cohomology with the Hom's out of X^i_st(M); since the filtration on M_K is concentrated in degree i, Example 5.11 of Corollary 5.10 finishes the proof.

items.name: Lemma 9.5: no G_K-maps out of the differentials
items.statement: Hom^{sm}_{G_K}((Ω^{i−1}_X/ker d) ⊗̂_K C,B_st) = 0 and Hom_{G_K}((Ω^{i−1}_X/ker d) ⊗̂_K C,B_dR) = 0. Since the smooth Hom is the colimit of Hom_{G_L} over finite L/K and B_st ↪ B_dR, it suffices to treat Hom_{G_L}(−,B_dR); that vanishes because Hom_{G_L}(C,B_dR) = 0 by Proposition 2.14(iv), and the untensored subspace is dense while the maps are required to be continuous.

items.name: Proposition 2.14: the Hom-computations in B_dR
items.statement: For arbitrary K: (i) Hom_{G_K}(C,C) ≅ K and Hom_{G_K}(C,C(j)) = 0 for j ≠ 0; (ii) Hom_{G_K}(B^+_dR,t^{−N}B^+_dR/t^kB^+_dR) ≅ K for N ≥ 0, k ≥ 1, compatibly in k; (iii) Hom_{G_K}(B^+_dR,B^+_dR) ≅ K and Hom_{G_K}(B_dR,B_dR) ≅ K; (iv) Hom_{G_K}(t^jB^+_dR/t^kB^+_dR,B_dR) = 0 and Hom_{G_K}(B^+_dR/t^kB^+_dR,B^+_dR/t^ℓB^+_dR) = 0 for ℓ > k.
items.note: (i) rests on Fontaine's theorem; the alternative proof of Fourquaux applies only when K is finite over Q_p. The companion statements over the VS-categories are Corollary 3.18 (Hom_VS out of a torsion B^+_dR-Module vanishes) and Lemma 3.26.

items.name: The quasi-compact case of Theorem 9.3, with (9.7)
items.statement: For X quasi-compact smooth dagger over K and r ≥ i set H̃^{r,i} := H̃^i_proét(X_C,Q_p(r)), F̃^{r,i} := H̃^i(F^r(RΓ_dR(X) ⊗̂_K B^+_dR)), X^{r,i} := (H^i_HK(X_C) ⊗̂_{F^nr} B^+_st)^{N=0,ϕ=p^r} and B^i := H^i_dR(X) ⊗̂_K B^+_dR; let Ã^{r,i} be the kernel of F̃^{r,i} → B^i, which is also canonically a subgroup of H̃^{r,i}, and form the quotients H̄^{r,i}, F̄^{r,i}. Lemma 9.6 kills the Hom's out of Ã^{r,i}, so the Hom's out of H̄^{r,i} and H̃^{r,i} agree; the hypothesis of de Rham slopes ≥ 0 makes Conjecture 6.21 available, and its sequence (6.22) induces (9.7) 0 → H̄^{r,i} → X^{r,i} ⊕ F̄^{r,i} → B^i → 0 and 0 → H̄^{r,i} → X^{r,i} → B^i/F̄^{r,i} → 0, all of whose terms are classical because F̄^{r,i} ⊂ B^i. This identifies H̄^{r,i} topologically with V^r_st(H^i_HK(X_C),H^i_dR(X)), and Corollary 5.10 finishes the proof. §9.1.3: the remaining small varieties are handled by the same argument, Conjecture 6.21 being available for them too.
items.note: B^i takes this form because for X defined over K one has H^i_dR(X_C/B^+_dR) ≅ H^i_dR(X) ⊗̂_K B^+_dR (Remark 1.5(i)).

items.name: Lemma 9.6: no G_K-maps out of the kernel Ã^{r,i}
items.statement: Hom^{sm}_{G_K}(Ã^{r,i},B_st) = 0 and Hom_{G_K}(Ã^{r,i},B_dR) = 0 for all i ≤ r. It is enough to prove the B_dR-statement for A^{r,i}; the long exact sequence ⋯ → DR^{r,i−1} → F^{r,i} → B^i → DR^{r,i} → ⋯ with DR^{r,i} := H^i((B^+_dR ⊗̂ RΓ_dR(X))/F^r) exhibits A^{r,i} as a quotient of DR^{r,i−1}, so it suffices to treat DR^{r,i} for i < r. That group is the i-th hypercohomology of the complex (B^+_dR/t^r) ⊗̂_K O_X → (B^+_dR/t^{r−1}) ⊗̂_K Ω^1_X → ⋯ → (B^+_dR/t) ⊗̂_K Ω^{r−1}_X, hence a quotient of the group Z^{r,i} of i-cocycles of the Čech double complex of a covering by dagger affinoids; and choosing a Banach basis (t^je_n) of B^+_dR/t^r over K lifted from one of C decomposes that complex as a completed direct sum of the t^je_n ⊗ DR^{r−j,•}_K, so that ∑_{j≤r}(t^{r−j}B^+_dR/t^rB^+_dR) ⊗_K Z^{j,i}_K → Z^{r,i} has dense image; Proposition 2.14 and continuity then give the vanishing.

items.name: Theorem 9.8: the pro-étale-to-de Rham comparison over C
items.statement: For X a smooth dagger variety over C with de Rham slopes ≥ 0 and i ≥ 0: Hom_TVS(H^i_proét(X,Q_p),B_st) ≅ Hom_{F^nr}(H^i_HK(X),B_st) as a B_st-module and Hom_TVS(H^i_proét(X,Q_p),B_dR) ≅ Hom_{B^+_dR}(H^i_dR(X/B^+_dR),B_dR) as a B_dR-module — so de Rham cohomology without its Hodge filtration and Hyodo–Kato cohomology without ϕ and N can be recovered from pro-étale cohomology despite the absence of a Galois action. Writing h(𝐌) := Hom_TVS(𝐌,𝐁_dR) and forming, for fixed r ≥ i, the TVS-valued 𝐇^{r,i}, 𝐅^{r,i}, 𝐗^{r,i}, 𝐁^i and the kernel 𝐀^{r,i} of 𝐅^{r,i} → 𝐁^i: the latter is a 𝐁^+_dR-Pair, hence contains a dense inductive limit of finite length 𝐁^+_dR-Modules and h(𝐀^{r,i}) = 0 by Corollary 3.18, giving h(𝐇̄^{r,i}) ≅ h(𝐇^{r,i}); smallness makes 0 → 𝐇̄^{r,i} → 𝐗^{r,i} → 𝐁^i/𝐅̄^{r,i} → 0 a sequence of BC's, and it is exact because on C-points it is the sequence proved exact in (9.7) from Conjecture 6.21. This identifies 𝐇̄^{r,i} with V^r_st(H^i_HK(X),t^{−r}𝐅̄^{r,i}), and Proposition 5.20 concludes.
items.note: This is Conjecture 1.8 proved, the introduction writing Hom_VS for Hom_TVS; Remark 6.13(ii) is the precedent for proper X. In the printed proof the objects are defined with X_C although X is already over C, and h(−) is introduced for "a Topological Pair", a term used nowhere else.

items.name: Remark 9.9: what cannot, and what can, be recovered over C
items.statement: (i) For X proper, H^i_proét(X,Q_p) is a finite dimensional Q_p-vector space with no extra structure, so it is hopeless to try to recover ϕ and N on H^i_HK(X) or the filtration on H^i_dR(X/B^+_dR) from Theorem 9.8. (ii) For a dagger affinoid the filtration is known — F^{i+k}H^i_dR(X/B^+_dR) = t^kH^i_dR(X/B^+_dR) — and (9.10) (H^i_HK(X) ⊗_{F^nr} B^+_st)^{N=0,ϕ=p^i} ≅ (H^i_HK(X) ⊗_{F^nr} B^+_cris)^{ϕ=p^i}; Lemma 5.17 then squeezes Hom_TVS((H^i_HK(X) ⊗ B^+_cris)^{ϕ=p^i},B^+_cris) between two copies of H^i_HK(X)^* ⊗_{F^nr} B^+_cris, so that the action of ϕ on H^i_HK(X) ⊗_{F^nr} C̆ can be recovered by tensoring and dualising. (iii) For a general smooth dagger variety over C, (ii) suggests that a sheafified version of ϕ and of the filtration might be recoverable, while recovering N seems out of reach by these methods.
items.note: Remark 1.9 of the introduction explains the obstruction structurally: the t^k𝐁^+_dR are all isomorphic as VS’s though the t^kB^+_dR are distinct as G_K-modules, and Conjecture 1.4 determines the sheaf on the curve but not the modification at ∞ that produced it.

items.name: Appendix A: three-space problems for topological vector spaces
items.statement: The appendix lists basic facts about extensions of Banach and Fréchet spaces for which the authors could not find references. All four propositions concern a short exact sequence 0 → W_1 → W → W_2 → 0 in the left heart LH(C_K) and assert that a property of the outer terms is inherited by the middle one. Here a banach is a Banach space over Q_p up to equivalence of norms, and reasonable means Fréchet or a compact inductive limit.

items.name: Proposition A.1: an extension of banachs is a banach
items.statement: If 0 → W_1 → W → W_2 → 0 is exact in LH(C_K) and W_1, W_2 are banachs, so is W. Choose an open lattice U ⊂ W small enough that U ∩ W_1 ⊂ W_1^+, which exists because every open lattice of W_1 is the trace of one of W by strictness; the image of U in W_2 is then open, hence contains p^nW_2^+, and replacing U by its intersection with the preimage of p^nW_2^+ and then by U + W_1^+ gives an exact sequence 0 → W_1^+ → U → p^nW_2^+ → 0. Completing W for the norm induced by U yields a banach W' = lim_n W/p^nU with a strict exact sequence and a continuous W → W' over the identity on W_1 and W_2, so the five lemma makes W → W' an isomorphism in LH(C_K).

items.name: Remark A.2: when the extension splits
items.statement: If K is spherically complete, or if W_1 and W_2 are separable — that is, have a dense subspace of countable dimension — then the sequence of Proposition A.1 splits. On the other hand it seems that for Ĉ_p a spherical completion of C_p the sequence of C_p-banachs 0 → C_p → Ĉ_p → Ĉ_p/C_p → 0 does not split; in particular the C_p-dual of Ĉ_p is 0.
items.note: The implication in the last sentence runs the other way round: it is the vanishing of the C_p-dual that would force non-splitting, since a splitting would give a nonzero continuous C_p-linear projection Ĉ_p → C_p. Both assertions are advanced tentatively ("it seems").

items.name: Proposition A.3: an extension of fréchets is a fréchet
items.statement: If 0 → W_1 → W → W_2 → 0 is exact in LH(C_K) and W_1, W_2 are fréchets, so is W. For a fréchet F with a decreasing basis (U_n) of open lattices the map F → lim_n F/U_n is an isomorphism; and for any open lattices U_1 ⊂ W_1, U_2 ⊂ W_2 one can build an open lattice U ⊂ W with U ∩ W_1 ⊂ U_1 and image in U_2, hence a decreasing family (U_n) whose images and traces are bases of neighbourhoods of 0 in W_2 and W_1. Then W' := lim_n W/U_n is a fréchet, with metric d(x,y) = p^{−n} for n least with x − y ∉ U_n, sitting in an exact sequence of fréchets over the identity on W_1 and W_2, so W → W' is an isomorphism in LH(C_K).

items.name: Proposition A.4: an extension of compact type spaces is of compact type
items.statement: If 0 → W_1 → W → W_2 → 0 is exact in LH(C_K), W_1 and W_2 are of compact type, and either K is spherically complete or W_1 and W_2 are separable, then W is of compact type. Passing to stereotypical duals gives 0 → W_2^* → W^* → W_1^* → Ext^1(W_2,K) → ⋯ with Ext^1(W_2,K) = 0 because W_2 is separated; since W_1^*, W_2^* are nuclear fréchets, W^* is a fréchet by Proposition A.3 and is nuclear by Dierolf–Roelcke. Dualising back gives a commutative diagram (A.5) whose outer vertical maps are isomorphisms — this is where the hypothesis on K or on separability is needed, since otherwise the duals could vanish — so the rows are exact and W → W' is an isomorphism in LH(C_K).
items.note: The hypothesis is printed as "K is spherically closed", a term used nowhere else in the paper; the proof of the same proposition and Remark A.2 both say spherically complete. Ext^1(W_2,K) = 0 is quoted from the authors' earlier work with Gilles, and the nuclearity from Dierolf–Roelcke.

items.name: Remark A.6: the extensions need not split
items.statement: The sequences of Propositions A.3 and A.4 have no reason to split, even for K finite over Q_p. Kohlhaase showed that the derivation d/dx : LA(Z_p) → LA(Z_p) on locally analytic functions, though surjective, has no continuous section, so the sequence of compact type spaces 0 → LC(Z_p) → LA(Z_p) → LA(Z_p) → 0 does not split; dually, with R^+ the ring of analytic functions on the open unit ball and t = log(1+T), the sequence of fréchets 0 → tR^+ → R^+ → R^+/t → 0 does not split.
